events.title: Pyrrhus lands
events.text: Answering Tarentum's call, he crosses with about 25,000 men and twenty elephants, though a storm scatters his fleet.

events.title: Battle of Heraclea
events.text: Elephants break the Roman line on the Siris; ancient figures for Pyrrhus's dead run from under 4,000 to 13,000.

events.title: Rhegium seized
events.text: The Campanian garrison Rome posted under Decius kills the men of Rhegium and takes the city.

events.title: March into Latium
events.text: Pyrrhus advances to within days of Rome, but its allies do not defect.

events.title: Appius Claudius speaks
events.text: The old, blind senator is carried into the Senate to speak against peace; Cineas's mission fails.

events.title: Battle of Asculum
events.text: Two days of fighting: another win so costly that it gives us the phrase 'Pyrrhic victory'.

events.title: Thoenon ousts Hicetas
events.text: After nine years, the ruler of Syracuse is overthrown, leaving the city split between rivals.

events.title: Mago off Ostia
events.text: Justin gives the Carthaginian admiral 120 ships; tradition places the fleet off Rome's port. The Senate declines his help.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: Polybius records a pact against Pyrrhus: Carthage supplies the ships, and no crew can be forced ashore.

events.title: Mago visits Pyrrhus
events.text: Days after leaving Rome, Mago goes to the king as a peacemaker, to learn his plans for Sicily.

events.title: Raid on Rhegium
events.text: Punic ships carry 500 Romans to Rhegium and burn timber stored for shipbuilding, then guard the Strait.

events.title: Siege of Syracuse
events.text: Diodorus counts 100 Carthaginian ships in the Great Harbour and 50,000 men outside the walls.

events.title: Fabricius warns Pyrrhus
events.text: Rome reveals a plot to poison the king, opening the way to a truce and an exchange of prisoners.

events.title: Pyrrhus sails
events.text: After two years and four months in Italy, he leaves a garrison at Tarentum and puts in at Locri.

events.title: Tauromenium joins
events.text: Its ruler Tyndarion gives Pyrrhus soldiers and his alliance.

events.title: Catana's golden crowns
events.text: The city welcomes the king with ceremony and crowns him with gold.

events.title: Syracuse relieved
events.text: With thirty Punic ships away on other duties, Pyrrhus sails into Syracuse unchallenged.

events.title: A fleet gained
events.text: Syracuse yields 120 decked ships, 20 open ones and a royal 'nine', lifting his fleet above 200.

events.title: Leontini offers troops
events.text: Its ruler Heracleides offers the city, its forts, 4,000 foot and 500 horse.

events.title: Enna expels garrison
events.text: The island's central stronghold drives out its Punic troops and offers Pyrrhus an alliance.

events.title: Acragas changes sides
events.text: Sosistratus gives Pyrrhus Acragas, thirty towns, 8,000 foot and 800 horse.

events.title: Heraclea Minoa falls
events.text: Pyrrhus marches into Carthage's province and takes its garrisoned town on the south coast.

events.title: Selinus and Halicyae
events.text: Diodorus lists these cities of the south-west among Pyrrhus's quick captures in Carthage's province.

events.title: Segesta goes over
events.text: The hill city of the Elymians, long tied to Carthage, falls into Pyrrhus's hands.

events.title: Eryx stormed
events.text: Carthage's strongest hill fortress falls; Plutarch has Pyrrhus first on the wall.

events.title: Iaetia surrenders
events.text: The hill town inland from Panormus gives itself up without a fight.

events.title: Panormus stormed
events.text: Carthage loses its finest harbour on the north coast.

events.title: Hercte taken
events.text: The stronghold near Panormus falls, leaving Carthage only Lilybaeum.

events.title: Mamertines beaten
events.text: Pyrrhus kills their tribute collectors, wins a battle and destroys many strongholds, but leaves Messana in their hands.

events.title: Rome takes Croton
events.text: While Pyrrhus is away, Rome recovers Croton and Locri, as his Italian allies weaken.

events.title: Carthage offers peace
events.text: Plutarch: money and ships, refused unless Carthage quits Sicily. Diodorus: he nearly concedes Lilybaeum.

events.title: Lilybaeum holds
events.text: New walls, towers, a ditch, supplies by sea and catapults defeat a two-month siege.

events.title: Oarsmen pressed
events.text: To invade Africa, Pyrrhus forces crews from the cities; Plutarch says the leader became a tyrant.

events.title: Thoenon executed
events.text: The man who handed over Syracuse's Island is killed on a charge of conspiracy.

events.title: Sosistratus flees
events.text: Warned that Pyrrhus means to seize him, the lord of Acragas gets away.

events.title: The cities revolt
events.text: Some Greek cities join Carthage, others the Mamertines; Pyrrhus's Sicilian realm falls apart.

events.title: Battle of the Strait
events.text: Appian: of 110 warships, Carthage sinks 70 and disables all but twelve of the rest. Plutarch says only 'many'.

events.title: Mamertine ambush
events.text: Crossing to Italy with thousands of Mamertines ahead, Pyrrhus loses two elephants and is wounded in the head.

events.title: Locri's temple plundered
events.text: Short of money, Pyrrhus takes Persephone's treasure; a storm drives it back and he restores it.

events.title: Battle of Beneventum
events.text: A night march goes astray and Curius attacks at dawn. Some moderns call it a draw, but it ends his war in Italy.

events.title: Hiero rises
events.text: At Syracuse, the army makes a young officer its general; he will rule for decades. The date is approximate.

events.title: Pyrrhus takes Macedonia
events.text: Home with 8,000 foot and 500 horse, he beats Antigonus Gonatas and his Gauls and takes most of the kingdom.

events.title: Sparta holds
events.text: Pyrrhus attacks Sparta; its women help dig the trench, and reinforcements arrive in time.

events.title: Death at Argos
events.text: Fighting at night in the streets, he is stunned by a tile thrown by an old woman and is beheaded.

events.title: Tarentum surrenders
events.text: His garrison gives up the city to Rome; Livy's summary says a Punic fleet came too, breaking the treaty.

chartNote: Share of the mapped area, by the main power in each present-day region; modern boundaries stand in for ancient ones, and every region is a simplification. Trapani stays Carthaginian throughout because Lilybaeum never fell, although Eryx, Segesta and Selinus inside it were taken in 277 BC. Northern Italy, outside the war, counts toward no power. Ancient dates for 278–276 BC are uncertain, and the Strait battle is sometimes put in 275 BC.
